title: CACPGB-Net: Dual-module network for wrestling action recognition
direction: 摔跤动作 / 相位识别
abstract: Freestyle wrestling technique recognition is hindered by close-range occlusion, entangled limbs, and phase structure that a generic frame encoder with temporal mean pooling does not protect. This paper proposes CACPGB-Net, a dual-module clip recognizer built on ResNet18 that inserts CoordAttContact after ResNet18 stage-4 feature maps, before global pooling and PhaseGateBiLSTM on the 16-frame embedding sequence after spatial pooling. CoordAttContact addresses coordinate attention that emphasizes elongated limb-contact structures, whereas PhaseGateBiLSTM targets phase-gated bidirectional LSTM that separates prepare/attack/finish phases. On the OpenFSW stratified split (train/val = 167/42) with 16-frame clips, the shared ResNet18 baseline reaches 80.95\% validation accuracy. Under the same protocol, the CoordAttContact-only and PhaseGateBiLSTM-only variants reach 83.33\% and 83.33\%, and the full CACPGB-Net model reaches 88.10\% (+7.14~pp). Four-variant ablation and a multi-method comparison suite support complementary module roles. freestyle wrestling, action recognition, OpenFSW, CoordAttContact, PhaseGateBiLSTM, ResNet18, temporal modeling, ablation study
